scenes.headline: How LongStraw fits million-token RL on eight GPUs
scenes.sub: Capture the prompt once, then replay one response at a time
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Scooter! RL post-training mostly stops at a quarter of a million tokens. LongStraw runs two-million-token steps on eight GPUs. Here's the trick.

scenes.text: Treat the long prompt as detached resident state, captured once without gradients, and replay one response at a time under autograd.
scenes.mark: replay one response at a time
scenes.say: The idea: treat the long prompt as detached state, captured once without gradients. Then replay one response at a time with autograd on.

scenes.title: Where the graph stops
scenes.say: GRPO scores several responses to one prompt, and all of them lean on the same long history. So LongStraw moves the graph boundary.

parts.note: the prompt's state, computed by the current weights
parts.say: Inside the brackets is the prompt's state: recurrent state and cache pages, only what later tokens need.

parts.note: no autograd: the prompt's activation graph is never kept
parts.say: It's evaluated with no autograd, so the prompt's huge activation graph is never kept.

parts.note: resident, read-only; its gradient term is dropped
parts.say: The catch: the gradient through the prompt is dropped. It trains on the response gradient only, and says full-sequence parity is not claimed.

items.text: Capture the prompt once, no autograd
items.say: Capture the long prompt once, keeping only the compact state later tokens need.
Score the old-policy and reference branches from that state, without building a graph.
Rebuild just one policy response with autograd on, and backpropagate through it.

items.text: Free the graph, replay the next
items.say: Free its graph and replay the next one. Group size now costs time, not memory.
One capture serves a step or two nearly for free. By step four the cached state has clearly gone stale.

scenes.label: more peak memory per rank going from G=2 to G=8
scenes.note: at 2,097,152 positions, Qwen3.6-27B on eight H20 GPUs
scenes.say: The payoff: at two million positions, going from two responses per group to eight adds only point two oh eight gigabytes per GPU.

scenes.text: Long-context RL is a state-lifetime and ownership problem, not an attention-kernel problem.

recap: Capture the long prompt once, as resident state
Replay one response graph at a time
Response-only gradients; the step executes, parity isn't claimed
scenes.say: To recap: capture once, replay one response at a time, and read it as a systems result, honestly labelled.
